status: Frozen before any held-out run or result. This file defines rules; it contains no results.
run_request_ids: Each run submits a copy of the case request with request_id '<case request_id>-<configuration id>-r<repetition>' and revision 1. No other request field changes.

clarification.answer_source: The case's clarification_answer, sent verbatim to every clarification question.
clarification.default_answer: No other requirements. Please continue with what I gave you.
clarification.after_max: The harness sends the default answer to later questions.

adjudicated_class.answerable: At least one valid offer meeting every hard constraint was found by any method during the case's evaluation window: any configuration or repetition, any baseline, or the verifier's own 10-minute search.
adjudicated_class.no_match_observed: No method found a valid offer meeting every hard constraint during the evaluation window.
adjudicated_class.rule: Scoring uses the adjudicated class. The designed outcome is a hypothesis; disagreements between designed and adjudicated classes are reported per case.

offer_verdicts.valid: Every hard constraint and decisive fact is confirmed at the retailer and the presented price and total match.
offer_verdicts.unverifiable_rule: An offer the verifier cannot check (blocked page, bot check, login wall) counts as invalid in the primary rate and is excluded in a labelled sensitivity rate.
offer_verdicts.drift_rule: If the run's own evidence shows the presented price but the live page differs at verification, the reason is price_drift. It is still invalid in the primary rate and is reported separately.

verification_plan.repetition_1: Every selected offer of every main recommendation is verified by hand.
verification_plan.repetitions_2_and_3: Automated re-observation of every selected offer plus human verification of a random 20% sample drawn with seed 78.
verification_plan.additional_sellers: Automated re-observation plus the 20% human sample in every repetition; reported as a secondary validity figure.
verification_plan.verifier: A teammate other than the operator of the run or session, where possible.
verification_plan.forbidden: No login, cart, checkout, seller contact or bot-check bypass. A cost shown only at checkout stays not shown.

decisive_facts: identity: every hard identity constraint (model, storage, memory, GPU, SIM, connectivity, model code)
retailer-reported stock for the requested fulfillment (pickup stock must be for the pickup location)
delivery or pickup charge for the case destination
other mandatory charges (tax treatment, card or cash surcharges, import and route charges)
payment method when the case requires one
warranty when the case requires one
deadline basis when the case has a deadline
seller market (a domestic case needs a seller in Lebanon)

metrics.question: Are the offers TechScout presents as verified recommendations actually valid?
metrics.numerator: Selected offers of main recommendations judged valid by human verification.
metrics.denominator: All selected offers of main recommendations (at most three per run) presented in repetition-1 runs of the configuration, over all 30 held-out cases. Unverifiable offers stay in the denominator.
metrics.aggregation: Ratio of totals, with a case-clustered bootstrap interval.
metrics.target_rule: Reported as met when the point estimate is at least 0.95; described as met with confidence only when the 95% interval's lower bound is also at least 0.95; not assessed when the denominator is below 20.
secondary: additional_seller_validity (automated re-observation plus a 20% human sample)

metrics.question: How often does a run end with the right outcome for the case?
metrics.numerator: Successful runs. On an answerable case: at least one valid selected offer, no invalid selected offer, finished within the time limit, no scope or constraint violation. On a no_match_observed case: no main recommendation, a stated reason naming the blocking constraint or missing facts, and no invented offer (labelled uncertain alternatives are allowed).
metrics.denominator: All runs of the configuration on all 30 cases, including errors, timeouts and cancellations.
metrics.aggregation: Mean of per-case success fractions, so each case weighs the same; case-clustered bootstrap interval.

metrics.question: When a valid offer exists, does the run deliver it?
metrics.numerator: Runs on answerable cases that meet the answerable success rule of request_success_rate.
metrics.denominator: All runs on adjudicated answerable cases. Abstaining on an answerable case counts as a failure, so abstention cannot raise this rate.
metrics.aggregation: Mean of per-case success fractions; case-clustered bootstrap interval.

metrics.question: How often does the run return no main recommendation?
metrics.numerator: Runs with zero main recommendations (any terminal status).
metrics.aggregation: Reported overall and split into correct abstention (no_match_observed cases) and unnecessary abstention (answerable cases), each with its own denominator. Runs that ended in error, timeout or cancellation are inside the numerator and are also reported as their own count, so failures are not mistaken for deliberate abstention.

metrics.question: On how many answerable cases does the configuration find a valid offer at all?
metrics.numerator: Answerable cases whose repetition-1 run has at least one valid selected offer.

metrics.question: How much of the valid market found by all methods did the configuration find?
metrics.numerator: Distinct valid seller offers (seller and exact configuration) the configuration presented as main recommendations or additional verified sellers.
metrics.denominator: Distinct valid seller offers found by any method for the case during its evaluation window.
metrics.aggregation: Mean over answerable cases; reported as exploratory because the pool depends on the methods run.

metrics.question: How many retailers did each run know, try, read and qualify?

definitions.discovered: Distinct canonical retailers (seller identities, not domains) identified as candidate sources for the run's category and market scope, from the directory, the corpus or runtime discovery.
definitions.attempted: Discovered retailers with at least one request-relevant retrieval dispatched through the source gate during the run.
definitions.retrieved: Attempted retailers with at least one usable response that produced a product record in the requested category.
definitions.qualifying: Retrieved retailers with at least one offer that passed eligibility and current-run verification (main recommendation, additional verified seller or expandable qualifying result).

metrics.denominator: Per run; aggregated as median and interquartile range per configuration and as the union of distinct retailers over the set, domestic and international reported separately.
metrics.consistency: discovered >= attempted >= retrieved >= qualifying, as in CoverageCounts. Retailers consulted only through stored corpus evidence are reported separately as corpus_consulted.

metrics.question: Does the run give a real multi-seller comparison?
metrics.numerator: Runs with at least one exact configuration offered by two or more distinct sellers whose offers are all verified and price-comparable.
metrics.also_report: Per-run count of such configurations (median and distribution).

metrics.question: How soon does the buyer first see something useful?
metrics.definition: From request submission to the first display (poll snapshot, result page or assistant reply) that shows a product matching the case's identity constraints with a price. TechScout provisional candidates count when the product matches, even before verification.
metrics.denominator: All runs or sessions; ones that never show a useful display are censored at their limit.
metrics.aggregation: p50 and p95 with censored runs ranked as slower than every observed time; a percentile is 'not reached' when censored runs cover it.

metrics.question: How long until a verified result exists?
metrics.definition: TechScout: from submission to the first snapshot with a verified main recommendation. External and manual baselines: from session start to the moment the operator has confirmed every decisive fact of the chosen offer at the retailer; the verification phase is logged separately as extra buyer effort.
metrics.denominator: All runs or sessions on answerable cases; others censored as above.
metrics.aggregation: p50 and p95 with censoring as above.

metrics.question: Does every run respect the 120-second active execution limit?
metrics.numerator: Runs whose recorded active execution is at most 120 seconds and whose results were published within it.

metrics.question: What does one successful request cost?
metrics.numerator: Marginal spend of all runs of the configuration on the held-out set, including failed runs (model, search, retrieval, embedding and retries, from the shared ledger).
metrics.also_report: Total spend and tokens per configuration and per agent role; corpus acquisition and maintenance cost as a separate fixed figure, never amortized silently.

metrics.question: Does every decisive claim cite evidence that supports it?
metrics.numerator: Selected offers whose decisive claims each link to a resolvable evidence excerpt that supports the claim, with price and stock evidence from the current run.
metrics.denominator: Selected offers of main recommendations in repetition-1 runs.

metrics.question: Does the run keep the buyer's constraints and default scope?
metrics.numerator: Runs with no silent relaxation (budget maximum, condition, storage or other hard field changed without the buyer choosing it) and no scope violation (a foreign purchase offer on a domestic case, or domestic results dropped on an international case when they exist).

metrics.question: For the identical item, who found the lower verified total?
metrics.rule: Win, tie and loss only when both sides have a valid offer for the identical configuration with price-comparable verified totals. Every other pair is counted in its own category.
metrics.scope: Domestic cases only. International cases, including H11 and H30 in the assistant subset, are reported in international_capability for every side and never enter paired price outcomes or domestic success comparisons.
metrics.savings: Among win, tie and loss pairs: the per-pair difference in USD (median and mean).
metrics.test: Exact two-sided sign test on wins versus losses; descriptive only at this sample size.

metrics.question: Does the system understand the buyer's wording?
metrics.numerator: Interpretation checks satisfied by the requirements the run displays or uses.
metrics.denominator: All interpretation checks of the cases in the language group, in repetition-1 runs.
metrics.aggregation: Reported separately for en, ar and arabizi with their case counts; no claim beyond the tested cases.

metrics.question: How often does the run ask the buyer a question?
metrics.definition: Number of clarification questions per run, reported per case; questions on cases with clarification_expected are listed separately.

metrics.question: What can the configuration do for international requests?
report: domestic results retained when a domestic valid offer exists
international offers found, by market and route type (direct or forwarded)
cost state of each foreign offer (verified total, estimated range, incomplete subtotal)
estimated or incomplete offers wrongly placed in main recommendations (each one is also an invalid offer)
foreign offers wrongly described as cheaper than a verified domestic total
metrics.denominator: Runs on the 7 international cases; reported apart from domestic comparisons.

metrics.question: What happened in each external or manual session?
metrics.denominator: All planned sessions of the service on its subset, including failed ones.

price_comparability.same_configuration: Both offers have confirmed hardware equivalence for every identity field the category requires (app.identity compare_offers). Known differences or unresolved identity make the pair not comparable.
price_comparability.same_condition: Both offers have the same condition. A refurbished offer is never a price win over a new one.
price_comparability.same_basis: Both totals cover the case's fulfillment (delivery to the case city, or pickup) and every mandatory charge.
price_comparability.cost_state: Only verified payable totals are compared. An estimated range or incomplete subtotal is never a win over a verified total.
price_comparability.currency: Compare in the shared currency. Different currencies are converted with one reference rate recorded per verification pass (Banque du Liban published rate, with URL and timestamp); if no rate is recorded, the pair is inconclusive.
price_comparability.time: Both offers are verified in the same verification pass. For an automated block or a paired session, the pass is the set of independent verifier checks for that case, each within 60 minutes of the run or session that presented the offer and all finished within 60 minutes after the last run or side of the block or session.
price_comparability.warranty: Differences in warranty terms do not block comparison but are listed with the pair.
price_comparability.tie_rule: A difference of at most the larger of USD 1.00 and 0.5% of the lower total is a tie.
price_comparability.needs_based: Different models are not price-compared. Needs-based fit and task success are reported separately from identical-item price outcomes.

timing.harness_rule: At the wall-clock limit the harness cancels the run and scores its latest snapshot. Results published after 120 seconds of active execution do not count.
timing.manual_shopping_rule: One phase of at most 20 minutes, verification included.

dated_cases.H27: Void and reported as such if run after 2026-12-24T18:00:00+02:00.

timing.clocks: Harness and operator timestamps are ISO 8601 with offset; durations come from one monotonic clock per session.

repetitions_and_clustering.rule: Repetitions are not independent requests. Per-case results are averaged over repetitions first; intervals resample cases.

statistics.interval: 95% percentile interval from a case-clustered bootstrap
predeclared_comparisons: full-warm versus single-agent-warm: request success, useful-result success, valid-offer rate, paired price outcomes, latency, cost per successful request
full-warm versus fixed-heuristic-warm: the same measures
full-warm versus full-cold: validity, coverage, freshness (age of the oldest decisive fact at verification), latency and cost per successful request
TechScout versus LebTech, One Souq and manual shopping on the local subset: paired price outcomes, request success, latency and buyer effort
TechScout versus browsing-enabled ChatGPT and Claude on the 10 domestic cases of the assistant subset: the same measures; H11 and H30 are reported only in international_capability
statistics.exploratory_rule: Any other comparison is labelled exploratory.
hypotheses: The valid-offer rate of full-warm is at least 0.95.
Full-warm has more paired price wins than losses against each AI baseline (single-agent-warm, chatgpt-browsing, claude-browsing).
These are hypotheses to test, not claims; they are reported whichever way the results fall.
statistics.separate_experiments: The broader-discovery experiment in #80 and any keyword-only versus hybrid retrieval comparison run on development cases and are reported apart from held-out outcomes; neither is part of this protocol.

change_control.before_pre_run_freeze: Changes need a version bump recorded with eval/freeze.py, a changelog reason and a PR. Held-out texts may change only to fix an error unrelated to answers, and never after anyone has seen a held-out output.
change_control.pre_run_freeze: Before the first held-out run, record eval/corpus/warm.json and eval/run-freeze.json with eval/freeze.py --pre-run.
change_control.after_first_heldout_run: The protocol, datasets and frozen settings do not change. Fixes create a new labelled post-freeze version whose results are reported apart from the original results.
change_control.no_peeking: No one runs TechScout, a baseline or a manual search on a held-out case before the pre-run freeze. Smoke tests and demos use calibration or development cases.
